$schema-note: HIMMEL-689 — delegation-lane registry. Consumed by scripts/lanes/resolve.mjs. Inventory here; invariant policy stays in CLAUDE.md.
$quota-note: quota.bank declares the machine-readable bank governing the lane (HIMMEL-1000 exporter fanout). quota.accessPaths models each economic access path separately; activeAccessPath selects the path this lane actually uses, and that path's windows are the only subscription limits allowed to gate it. Lanes without quota are dashboard-omitted.
$readiness-note: readiness.passesRequired (HIMMEL-1626) = the lane must show this many TRAILING consecutive verify-return PASS rows (HIMMEL-1621 ledger) before guard-implementor-dispatch routes work toward it — readiness is measured, not asserted. Absent = always ready. Current gates carry the 2026-08-07 operator rulings: glm down until 10 consecutive passes (HIMMEL-1575 startup-hang class); claudex on probation, 5 consecutive passes graduate it.
$dispatch-note: HIMMEL-1942 — every impl lane declares kind=session|oneshot, command argv, generic flag mappings, brief delivery, workspace ownership, and timeoutSeconds. Session means a persistent worker result/session shape; workspaceOwner records whether the lane chokepoint or dispatcher provisions it. lanes.local.json may deep-overlay dispatch, including nested flags. defaultImplLane (registry or lanes.local.json overlay) selects a lane after --lane and HIMMEL_IMPL_LANE; the field is intentionally ABSENT here — every dispatch lane in this registry is impl-dormant by operator ruling (2026-08-19, HIMMEL-1967: pure Claude Code native), so an unqualified impl dispatch must refuse toward the native-subagent path rather than silently default to one.
$context-note: context.windowTokens + context.overflow (HIMMEL-1029/HIMMEL-1768) are the single structured source for /lanes context prose. overflow=compact-continue means the lane remains usable after the operating window by compacting, at a cost/churn penalty; overflow=hard-limit means work must fit. Absent = unverified/varies. Sources: Claude tiers per model catalog (Haiku 4.5 200k; Sonnet / Opus / Fable 1M); GLM = z.ai glm-5.2[1m], a real 1M lane. All FIVE codex-family lanes now read 900000 (HIMMEL-1833, operator ruling 2026-08-17) — the evidence backing that number is NOT uniform across the five, and this note exists so a future reader can see which are measured vs. ruled, not to flatten them into one story. `hermes-oneshot` defaults to whatever the himmel_agent hermes profile currently sets, NOT a pinned id: as of 2026-08-22 that is `stealth/ox-alpha` (provider `nous`, base_url https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1) — free, front-tier, and TEMPORARY availability; it was gpt-5.6-sol. Re-measured on ox-alpha (HIMMEL-2024, 2026-08-22): synthetic accept probes at 300K / 600K / 900K tokens ALL accepted (43.0s / 49.1s / 35.5s wall), with no context_length_exceeded and no rejection text at any size, so the probe gave no reason to LOWER 900000 — but it is not an independent confirmation of a usable 900K window either. 900000 remains what it already was before ox-alpha: an operator ruling/measurement (HIMMEL-1833), and the probe only establishes that the request is ACCEPTED at that size. Caveat carried over from `overflow: compact-continue`: an accepted probe does not prove the model attended to every token — the 900K probe returned FASTER than the 600K one, which is what compaction upstream of the model looks like, so treat 900000 as the declared operating window, not a measured attention ceiling. SUPERSEDED evidence: hermes previously live-verified accepts up to ~371K and rejects ~382K+ with context_length_exceeded — 350000 left ~22K margin (hermes-agent commit 522997543, 2026-08-16). CURRENT: the operator upgraded hermes and measured ~900K as what was actually attainable, at hermes v0.20.2 (2026.8.16), upstream commit bab7be3c (2026-08-17) — upstream reportedly raised the cap to 1M, the operator verified 900K in practice, and 900000 is the number to use; this is the only one of the five backed by a fresh, direct, operator-run measurement. `claudex` runs gpt-5.6-sol through CLIProxyAPI (scripts/claude-codex), not the codex CLI or hermes. Historically (pre-HIMMEL-1833) neither figure above transferred directly, but a THIRD independent source converged with the pre-raise 350000: the launcher's own `CODEX_CONTEXT_WINDOW` knob (previously defaulted 272000, a deliberate 2x-billing-cliff choice, not a hard ceiling) documented the real backend window as ~372k (~353k effective, citing openai/codex#32486) — within ~1-2% of hermes' 350000. That convergence is why 272000 was trusted rather than folklore. The lane's declared window (context.windowTokens) is now raised to 900000 on the SAME operator ruling that raised hermes-oneshot — the operator was shown this doubles billing past the old cliff and said "the cost is changing, let's go with it." But the CLIProxyAPI path itself is UNMEASURED at 900K — the hermes 900K figure does not transfer here any more than the old 350K one did automatically; this is an open, named gap, not an oversight. The launcher's own `CODEX_CONTEXT_WINDOW` default is deliberately left at 272000 rather than moved to match — its own code already WARNS above the ~372k backend-window ceiling it has evidence for on this path, so setting it to 900000 by default would trigger that warning on every dispatch, not confirm the lane is safe there. `CODEX_CONTEXT_WINDOW` remains a genuine per-invocation-overridable lever for a caller who wants to opt UP toward the ruled 900k figure and accept the risk, or stay at the evidence-backed 272000/353000 range. `codex` (paid, via hermes), `codex-exec`, `codex-wsl` all pin model gpt-5.5, not 5.6 — hermes measured this same gpt-5.5 pin genuinely REJECTS a 360K probe, so 272000 was a real, verified cap for these three, not a stale advertisement. Raised to 900000 anyway by explicit operator ruling (HIMMEL-1833, 2026-08-17): the operator was shown this exact conflict — gpt-5.5 rejecting 360K yet the lane now declaring 900000 — and chose to raise regardless. Recorded here as a RULING, not a measurement: these three are the LEAST-verified of the five raised lanes. If a gpt-5.5 dispatch on any of these three starts failing with context_length_exceeded around ~272K, that is the expected failure mode this note predicts, not a surprise. Two OTHER levers existed for claudex specifically for verifying the CLIProxyAPI path on its own evidence (as distinct from the operator-ruling override above) — (a) remains UNTESTED, not refuted; (b) is now APPLIED: (a) the `gpt-5.6-sol[1m]` model-name suffix — Claude Code's own documented convention is to STRIP `[1m]` before the provider ever sees it, so a direct curl of CLIProxyAPI with the suffix already attached (`HTTP 400 unknown provider for model gpt-5.6-sol[1m]`, probed 2026-08-17) tests a request shape Claude Code never actually sends and settles nothing about the real path through Claude Code — recorded here so nobody re-probes the wrong layer and mistakes it for an answer; (b) `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS` — an official, documented, name-independent Claude Code env var for declaring an unrecognized model's window, distinct from `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` (which only sets the compaction threshold) — APPLIED (HIMMEL-1887): the launcher now exports it, tied to `CODEX_CONTEXT_WINDOW`; the effective compact window is min(modelWindow, configured) and the out-of-catalog modelWindow fallback is a hardcoded 200000, so `CODEX_CONTEXT_WINDOW` was inert (silently clamped to 200k) until this export declared the window; both env vars get the SAME value so the clamp is structurally unreachable (guard: scripts/parity/test-launcher-context-env-parity.sh).
